rv.q: To change David Lindsay-Abaire’s poignant 2001 comedy into this fresh and gorgeous musical required this same deep-play, letter-by-letter concentration.
Kimberly Akimbo is the best new musical of 2021, and Jessica Stone's well-cast world-premiere production at the Atlantic does it justice.
“Kimberly Akimbo” is already the rare example of a good play that has become an even better musical.
This is a momentous work of theatre, exquisitely performed by a stellar cast of talent, known and new.
Jeanine Tesori’s music grounds the story in a way that gives the source material resonance, makes it more substantial and far more emotionally engaging.
How the two deal with the challenges presented make for two of the most exciting evenings in the New York theater season so far.

At a time when so many musicals feel so standardized, here's a show with a screw-loose point of view underscored by a real poignancy, created by writers with a solid understanding of musical theatre craft.
David Lindsay-Abaire and Jeanine Tesori have written one of the best shows of the season.
Any musical ending as strong as this does is lucky, for sure.
Watching a new show that satisfies and surprises never gets old.
Kimberly Akimbo is still worthwhile viewing, with a cast that couldn't be better.
In its quieter moments, Kimberly Akimbo displays a poignancy and tenderness that will seep into your heart.
The awkward, wry, tacitly sorrowful but explicitly exuberant relationship that slowly develops is the heart of the musical.

"If you didn't see the play, also by Lindsay-Abaire, you'll probably be delighted by Kimberly Akimbo's wacky story and tuneful score. But if you remember the original, you may be surprised by what you see onstage.
This is what needs to come to Broadway.
It’s a down to earth performance that elevates this quirky enterprise to surprising heights.
This show full of outcasts, strivers and one seriously ill young girl is anything but a downer; it’s carried along by spirited performances and a hopeful, compassionate sensibility.
Even with a few shortcomings this is a musical that will entertain and impress even the most discerning theatre goer.

cn.t: Critics embrace this funny, moving musical adaptation as a triumph, praising Victoria Clark's remarkable performance and the skillful transformation of Lindsay-Abaire's play into a bittersweet, offbeat gem with Tesori's tuneful score.
